TEXT_D:
Summary of 2019 UK policy proposals (max 500 words)

- Europe and constitutional reform
  - Revoke Article 50 to remain in the EU if winning a majority; otherwise back a referendum with an option to remain.
  - Protect freedom of movement; enfranchise long‑term EU residents in UK elections; reform electoral registration to automatic inclusion.
  - Electoral reform to Single Transferable Vote for MPs and councils; votes at 16; overseas constituencies; House of Lords reform; stricter transparency and regulation of political advertising and lobbying; citizens’ assemblies on major issues.
  - Devolution to nations and English regions with a written federal constitution and matched funding powers.

- Economy, business and work
  - £130bn infrastructure plan (transport, energy, schools, hospitals, housing), plus a £50bn regional rebalancing programme and Green Investment Bank.
  - Raise R&D to 3% of GDP; expand Catapult centres; regional innovation funds; support creative industries.
  - Skills Wallets of £10,000 per adult for lifelong learning; broaden apprenticeship levy to a Skills and Training Levy.
  - Corporate governance reforms: employee board representation; due‑diligence duties on human rights/environment; binding shareholder votes on executive pay.
  - Tax: restore Corporation Tax to 20%; replace Business Rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; align capital gains with income tax; tougher anti‑avoidance and improved Digital Services Tax.
  - Work: new “dependent contractor” status with core rights; living wage approach; flexible working from day one; stronger enforcement; fair gig‑economy pensions and zero‑hours protections.

- Education and childcare
  - Free, high‑quality childcare: 35 hours/week, 48 weeks/year for ages 2–4 and from 9–24 months for working parents; increased early years funding and staff training; expanded Children’s Centres.
  - Reverse school funding cuts; hire 20,000 teachers; clear repairs backlog.
  - Replace SATs and narrow league tables with broader assessment; new inspectorate; stronger SEND funding.
  - “Curriculum for life,” arts protection, careers links, better vocational routes.
  - Further/higher education: +£1bn for colleges, restore maintenance grants, stronger student mental health, review finance; Young People’s Premium.

- Environment, energy and transport
  - Net‑zero by 2045; at least 80% of electricity from renewables by 2030; ban fracking.
  - Ten‑year nationwide home insulation and zero‑carbon heat programme; zero‑carbon new buildings by 2021, rising to Passivhaus by 2025.
  - Circular economy law: phase out non‑recyclable single‑use plastics; right‑to‑repair; 70% recycling target.
  - Nature recovery targets; 60m trees/year; peatland and marine protection; £5bn flood programme; sustainable farming reform.
  - Transport: Clean Air Act; all new cars/vans electric by 2030; more ULEZs; rail electrification by 2035; fare freeze for a parliament; expand light rail, buses, cycling/walking; fix fares and access.

- Health, social care and public health
  - +1p on Income Tax raising £7bn/year for NHS and social care; £10bn capital; plan for a dedicated Health and Care Tax; integrate services and end automatic tendering.
  - Mental health: new waiting‑time standards; 24/7 crisis care; perinatal support; free prescriptions for chronic conditions; student mental health charter; tighter gambling rules.
  - Prevention: obesity strategy; right to clean air; minimum unit pricing for alcohol; PrEP on NHS; decriminalise abortion UK‑wide with safe access zones; drug policy reform including a regulated cannabis market.

- Social security, housing and communities
  - Reform Universal Credit: first payment in 5 days; end two‑child limit and benefit cap; higher work allowances incl. second earner; replace sanctions with incentive‑based approach; abolish bedroom tax; align LHA with rents; reinstate Independent Living Fund; right to food; end fuel poverty by 2025.
  - Pensions: retain triple lock; remedy for women born in the 1950s.
  - Housing: build 300,000 homes/year incl. 100,000 for social rent; zero‑carbon standards; Rent‑to‑Own; longer tenancies; licensing; curb second homes; end rough sleeping; repeal Vagrancy Act.
  - Rural/coastal: bus and rural services funds; universal superfast broadband and wider mobile coverage; coastal change fund.

- Policing, justice and rights
  - £1bn for community policing; public‑health approach to serious violence; £500m for youth services; Online Crime Agency; reform stop and search; replace Police and Crime Commissioners with local boards.
  - Reduce reoffending: more prison officers; presumption against short sentences; decriminalise possession for personal use; Women’s Justice Board; fair disclosure rules; strong rehabilitation on release.
  - Rights: protect Human Rights Act/ECHR; restore Legal Aid (£500m); halt police facial recognition; data/AI ethics code; no‑fault divorce; cohabiting rights; comprehensive equality measures incl. gender recognition reform, BSL Act, period poverty action, parental leave reform and pay‑gap transparency.

- Immigration and asylum
  - End the hostile environment; 28‑day limit on detention; move visa policy out of the Home Office to specialist departments; flexible work and post‑study visas; lower/waived fees; fair family rules.
  - Asylum: right to work after 3 months; resettle 10,000 vulnerable refugees annually and 10,000 unaccompanied children over 10 years; faster, higher‑quality decisions; free English lessons; longer move‑on period.

- Foreign policy and defence
  - Support multilateral institutions; maintain 0.7% aid with stronger focus on climate, gender and human rights; Magnitsky‑style sanctions; tighter arms export controls (including suspensions to rights‑abusing conflicts).
  - Parliamentary votes on military action; NATO 2% spending; bolster cyber capabilities; maintain a minimum nuclear deterrent (reduced fleet, altered posture).

TEXT_E:
Summary of commitments and policies (ideological language removed; no parties or individuals named)

- Brexit and trade: Implement the negotiated exit, leave EU law, the single market and customs union; no extension of the implementation period beyond December 2020. Pursue a free trade agreement with the EU and new deals with the USA, Australia, New Zealand and Japan; aim for 80% of UK trade to be covered by FTAs within three years. Create up to 10 freeports. Maintain UK standards; the NHS not part of trade talks.

- Economy, tax and cost of living: No increases to the main rates of income tax, National Insurance or VAT; raise the NI threshold to £9,500 with an ambition for £12,500 tax-free income. National Living Wage to two-thirds of median earnings by 2024 (forecast ~£10.50). £1bn for childcare before/after school and holidays. Keep pensioner benefits including the triple lock. Tighten anti–tax avoidance (new HMRC unit, tougher penalties) and introduce a Digital Services Tax. Fiscal rules cap public investment at an average 3% of GDP.

- NHS and social care: Record funding uplift; 50,000 more nurses; 6,000 more GPs plus 6,000 other primary care professionals; 50 million more GP appointments a year. 40 new hospitals and 20 upgrades; Innovative Medicines Fund; mental health reform for parity of esteem; hospital parking concessions for those most in need. Fast-track NHS visa. Social care: at least £1bn extra per year, cross-party reform with a guarantee no one has to sell their home to pay for care; carers’ leave of one week; double dementia research funding.

- Education and skills: Additional £14bn for schools with minimum per-pupil funding; teacher starting salary to £30k; behaviour support; “arts premium”; more SEND funding and places. National Skills Fund (£3bn), FE estate upgrade (£2bn), 20 Institutes of Technology; UK Shared Prosperity Fund to replace EU funds (including £500m for disadvantaged people’s skills).

- Policing and justice: 20,000 extra police officers; targeted knife crime orders; tougher sentences and end automatic halfway release for serious crimes; 10,000 more prison places; cyber crime force and a National Crime Laboratory; review parole; Royal Commission on criminal justice; Victims’ Law; Domestic Abuse Bill; online safety legislation.

- Immigration: Australian-style points system; equal approach to EU and non‑EU; NHS and top talent fast-track routes; five-year qualification period for most benefits; higher health surcharge; stronger enforcement and integration (including English language).

- Housing: Support long-term fixed-rate mortgages; discounted homes for local people; maintain Right to Buy; extend Help to Buy to 2023; reform shared ownership and leasehold. End “no-fault” evictions and introduce a single “lifetime” tenant deposit. Target 300,000 homes a year by mid‑2020s; “infrastructure first” via a £10bn fund; building safety reforms; protect green belt; tree-lined new streets. End rough sleeping by end of Parliament; stamp duty surcharge on non‑resident buyers.

- Infrastructure and connectivity: Towns Fund, cultural and community ownership funds. Major rail upgrades (including Northern Powerhouse Rail and Midlands Rail Hub), rail reform, restoration of some Beeching lines, superbus networks and electric buses. £1bn rapid EV charging network; consult on earliest phase‑out date for new petrol/diesel cars. £350m cycling fund and universal Bikeability. Gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025 with £5bn for hard‑to‑reach areas. Minimum transport service during strikes.

- Business and innovation: Business rates review and cuts (retail, pubs, small cinemas, music venues); higher Employment Allowance; crackdown on late payments; expand start‑up loans. Increase SME R&D tax credit to 13%; review Entrepreneurs’ Relief; improve support for the self‑employed. Increase R&D to 2.4% of GDP, create a high‑risk research agency, invest in data/health research, science clusters, and a 2022 UK innovation festival.

- Rural, farming and fisheries: Replace CAP with “public money for public goods”; farm budget guaranteed during the Parliament; expand seasonal workers scheme to 10,000. Leave the Common Fisheries Policy, manage stocks sustainably, and support coastal regeneration. Improve rural broadband/mobile and buses; tackle rural crime.

- Environment and climate: Environment Bill with an independent watchdog; Nature for Climate Fund (£640m) for trees and peatland; new protected landscapes. Plastics measures, extended producer responsibility, deposit return scheme, ban most plastic waste exports. Net Zero by 2050; offshore wind to 40GW by 2030; first carbon capture cluster by mid‑2020s (£800m); £500m to decarbonise heavy industry; support hydrogen and nuclear (including fusion); fracking moratorium; £9.2bn for energy efficiency; stronger air quality laws; £500m Blue Planet Fund.

- Union, devolution and democracy: Strengthen devolution; UK Shared Prosperity Fund to at least match EU funding by nation; constitutional review via a Commission; repeal Fixed-term Parliaments Act; retain First Past the Post and voting age 18; voter ID and postal vote safeguards; restore full voting rights for UK expats; protect free speech (including media reforms).

- Defence, foreign policy and veterans: Exceed NATO 2% with 0.5% real annual growth; modernise forces, create Space Command, invest in cyber; maintain nuclear deterrent; support UK defence industry. New legal protections and support for veterans, NIC relief for employers hiring them, childcare, railcard, guaranteed public‑sector interviews. Maintain 0.7% aid; Magnitsky sanctions; promote girls’ education, media freedom, anti‑slavery; aim to end preventable maternal/child deaths by 2030; build the UK Holocaust Memorial.

- Animal welfare: Tougher cruelty sentences; crack down on puppy smuggling; animal sentience law; end excessively long journeys for slaughter; extend ivory ban; ban trophy imports and primates as pets; advance cat microchipping and measures against pet theft.
